facts.fact: The National Registration Act, 1986 (No. 26), an Act of the Parliament of Botswana assented on 24 December 1986, commenced on 31 December 1986 and sets up a national register of citizens and lawfully resident non-citizens aged 16 or over, kept by the Registrar of National Registration, with an identity card issued to each registered person.

The Act requires every applicant to submit to fingerprinting and photographing, requires finger print records to go to the Registrar of National Registration, and gives each registrant a registration number in the national register, so the register it sets up is biometric.

systems.owner: Parliament of Botswana; Minister responsible for Home Affairs
